dev-ans00.content: The authors experimented with ILP-based summarization and several algorithms provided by the Sumy package. The ILP-based approach was compared with the Sumy algorithms [1].

dev-ans01.content: The word-level model baseline is not explicitly named in the sources, but the character-level model baseline is MemNNs (Memory Neural Networks) [2].

dev-ans02.content: No [1]. The paper mentions that this is the first attempt to introduce a common evaluation methodology for MRC gold standards, but it does not indicate that any corrections have been made to the gold standards based on their findings.

dev-ans03.content: They use an encoder with several convolutional layers followed by NIN layers and deep bidirectional LSTM at the higher part, and a decoder with a standard deep unidirectional LSTM with global attention [1].

dev-ans04.content: I can't find this in the papers.

dev-ans05.content: They used the Asian Scientific Paper Excerpt Corpus (ASPEC) [1] and the NTCIR PatentMT Parallel Corpus [1].

dev-ans08.content: The 18 propaganda techniques are listed in the paper but not explicitly named in the provided sources. The paper refers to a list of techniques that can be found in news articles and can be judged intrinsically, without the need to retrieve supporting information from external resources [1]. For the exact list, refer to BIBREF10 [1].

dev-ans09.content: The average length of the sentences is 15.5 words [1].

dev-ans10.content: They test Bernoulli embeddings (b-emb) BIBREF1 , continuous bag-of-words (CBOW) BIBREF5 , Distributed Memory version of Paragraph Vector (PV-DM) BIBREF11 and the Global Vectors (GloVe) BIBREF6 model [2].

dev-ans11.content: The machine learning based approaches compared are Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), Naive Bayes Classifier (NBC), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Gradient Boosting Classifier (GBC), Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD), K Nearest Neighbour (K-NN) and Random Forest (RF) [1].

dev-ans13.content: No, it is not valid to presume a bad medical Wikipedia article should not contain much domain-specific jargon. The paper indicates that domain-specific features, such as Domain Informativeness and Category, are crucial for improving the classification of medical articles, suggesting that domain-specific jargon is relevant and should be present [3]. Additionally, the extraction of bio-medical entities and the use of domain dictionaries are emphasized as important techniques for evaluating medical articles [2].

dev-ans14.content: NeuronBlocks includes the following neural network modules: RNN, CNN, QRNN, Transformer, Highway network, Encoder Decoder architecture, Linear/Bi-linear Attention, Full Attention, Bidirectional attention flow, Dropout, Layer Norm, Batch Norm, Focal Loss, AUC, Accuracy, Precision/Recall, F1, MSE/RMSE, and ExactMatch [1]. These modules are part of the Block Zoo, which provides a gallery of alternative layers/modules for constructing complex network architectures [4].

dev-ans15.content: Global context refers to the representation of the entire document, while local context refers to the representation of the topic or section within the document [3]. The combination of these two contexts is used to determine whether a sentence should be included in the summary [1].

dev-mul00.content: The speech recognition papers train or evaluate on LibriSpeech [1], Wall Street Journal (WSJ) [1], TED-LIUM2 [2], Spoken-SQuAD [3], and Mapudungun dialogues [5].

dev-mul01.content: The speech recognition systems in these papers are built for Vietnamese and Mapudungun [1][5].

dev-una00.content: The use of morphological segmentation improved the efficacy of the attention mechanism [1].

dev-una01.content: A node in the network approach represents a state. This is indicated by the description of the vote-speech layered network as a node-aligned undirected multilayer network where nodes correspond to states [2].

dev-una02.content: The RKS approach achieved a maximum accuracy of 99.53% using Fasttext features, which is a benchmarking result when compared to the literature [4]. The top 5 teams of sub-task A achieved a maximum f1-score of 82.9% [1]. The RKS approach improved the results compared to other methods [5].

dev-una03.content: The performance reported for the best models is 4.85% WER on the VLSP 2018 data set and 15.09% WER on the VLSP 2019 data set [1].
